cases.answer: Adding TyG to the clinical model plus CAD-RADS 2.0 did not significantly improve prognostic discrimination for MACE. The C-statistic increased from 0.731 to 0.733, an absolute increase of 0.002 (p = 0.505). This was assessed in 3528 patients with suspected or known CAD over a median follow-up of 50.4 months.

claims.claim: Adding TyG to the clinical model plus CAD-RADS 2.0 increased the C-statistic by only 0.002, from 0.731 to 0.733, without statistical significance (p = 0.505).
claims.quote:
However, both the addition of TyG index to clinical model plus CAD-RADS and to clinical model 
plus CAD-RADS 2.0 slightly but not significantly increased the C-statistic index (0.725 vs. 0.721, p = 0.223; 0.733 
vs. 0.731, p = 0.505).

claims.claim: The study included 3528 patients with suspected or known CAD.
claims.quote:
in patients with suspected or known coronary artery disease (CAD). The present study ultimately 
includes 3528 patients who met the enrollment criteria.

claims.claim: The discrimination outcome was MACE, with a median follow-up of 50.4 months.
claims.quote:
C-statistic was performed to assess the discriminatory value of models. 212 (6.0%) 
patients developed MACE during a median follow-up of 50.4 months (IQR, 39.4–55.1).

other_candidates.quote:
The addition of 
CAD-RADS 2.0 to clinical model plus CAD-RADS increased the C-statistic index significantly (0.731 vs. 0.721, 
p = 0.046).
other_candidates.why_rejected: This significant increase concerns adding CAD-RADS 2.0 to the clinical model plus CAD-RADS, not adding TyG.

other_candidates.quote:
Gao et al.28 revealed a significant improvement of risk evaluation after adding TyG index to 
clinical model in 1093 patients with coronary chronic total occlusion (AUC, 0.7244 vs. 0.629, p < 0.001).
other_candidates.why_rejected: This cited study assessed a different population and a clinical model without the specified CAD-RADS 2.0 comparison.

cases.answer: No randomized head-to-head evidence establishes that superiority. All included trials were placebo-controlled, so the network meta-analysis compared drug classes indirectly through placebo. In HFpEF, it found no significant differences among SGLT2 inhibitors, incretin-based therapies and finerenone for cardiovascular mortality or all-cause mortality.

claims.claim: The network meta-analysis used placebo-controlled trials and indirect comparisons between classes, rather than randomized head-to-head evidence.
claims.quote:
Because all included trials were placebo-
controlled, comparisons between treatment classes were 
derived through indirect evidence using placebo as the 
common comparator.

claims.claim: The article explicitly states that head-to-head trial evidence is lacking.
claims.quote:
class-level estimates 
against placebo show overlapping confidence intervals, 
and head-to-head trial evidence is lacking.

claims.claim: The HFpEF network meta-analysis found no significant between-class differences for cardiovascular or all-cause mortality.
claims.quote:
In the HFpEF NMA, there were no significant differ -
ences between any of the drug classes for CV mortality, 
all-cause mortality, or HF hospitalization/event.

claims.claim: The compared classes were SGLT2 inhibitors, incretin-based therapies and finerenone.
claims.quote:
Similarly, for the kidney composite outcome, no significant 
difference was observed between SGLT2i and finerenone, 
and no data were available for incretin-based therapies.

other_candidates.quote:
Among individuals with HFpEF, SGLT2i were associated 
with a statistically significant reduction in time to first 
HF hospitalization/event across the DL, REML-modified 
HK, and REML-Wald models.
other_candidates.why_rejected: This concerns HF hospitalization/events in placebo comparisons, not mortality superiority over other classes.

other_candidates.quote:
SGLT2i demonstrated 
superior efficacy in reducing both HF hospitalization 
and kidney composite outcome compared to incretin-
based therapies in T2D with ASCVD/high CV risk and 
CKD subgroups.
other_candidates.why_rejected: These indirect comparisons concern hospitalization and kidney outcomes in different populations, not HFpEF mortality.
